_title: The Most Scenic Train Rides in China: Karst Peaks, Rainbow Mountains and the Tibetan Plateau — WoW Train · glosx.app
_desc: The most beautiful train journeys in China, from Guilin’s karst peaks and the Yellow Mountain to Zhangye’s rainbow mountains, Qinghai Lake and the Hainan coast, with real journey times from Klook.
b1: The Most Scenic Train Rides in China: Karst Peaks, Rainbow Mountains and the Tibetan Plateau
b2: By WoW Train · November 2026 · 6 min read
b3: High-speed lines in China run through some extraordinary landscapes: limestone peaks, rice terraces, deserts, snowy plateaus and tropical coasts. These are the most scenic train rides, each with the fastest journey time and the number of trains we found on Klook.
b5: Guangzhou → Guilin · from 2h04 · 69 trains on the day we checked. Guilin is the gateway to the karst peaks of the Li River and to Yangshuo.
b6: Hangzhou → Huangshan · from 1h13 · 55 trains on the day we checked. Huangshan, the Yellow Mountain, is famous for its granite peaks, pines and seas of cloud.
b7: Changsha → Zhangjiajie · from 1h45 · 41 trains on the day we checked. Zhangjiajie, with the sandstone pillars of its national forest park, is under two hours from Changsha.
b8: Guiyang → Guilin · from 1h34 · 61 trains on the day we checked. A high-speed ride through the karst country of Guizhou and Guangxi.
b9: The far west: rainbow mountains and the plateau
b10: Lanzhou → Zhangye · from 2h08 · 51 trains on the day we checked. Zhangye, on the old Silk Road, is famous for the striped rainbow mountains of its Danxia landforms.
b11: Lanzhou → Xining · from 56 min · 89 trains on the day we checked. Xining, at the edge of the Tibetan Plateau, is the gateway to Qinghai Lake and Kumbum Monastery.
b12: Kunming → Lijiang · from 3h29 · 12 trains on the day we checked. Lijiang’s old town and the Jade Dragon Snow Mountain are about three and a half hours from Kunming.
b13: Kunming → Dali · from 1h55 · 95 trains on the day we checked. Dali, with its old town and Erhai Lake, is about two hours from Kunming.
b15: Xi'an → Chengdu · from 3h05 · 72 trains on the day we checked. The high-speed line crosses the Qinling Mountains, linking the city of the Terracotta Army with the home of the giant pandas.
b16: Chengdu → Guiyang · from 3h01 · 92 trains on the day we checked. The line runs south through the mountains to Guiyang, the base for the Huangguoshu Waterfall and the Miao villages of Guizhou.
b17: Chongqing → Kunming · from 4h51 · 22 trains on the day we checked. A mountain line from Chongqing to Kunming, the gateway to the Stone Forest and the rest of Yunnan.
b18: Wuhan → Yichang · from 1h34 · 80 trains on the day we checked. Yichang is the gateway to the Three Gorges Dam and the start of many Yangtze cruises.
b20: Haikou → Sanya · from 1h14 · 215 trains on the day we checked. The high-speed line along Hainan’s east coast links the island’s capital with the beaches of Sanya.
b21: Shenyang → Dalian · from 1h25 · 76 trains on the day we checked. Dalian, a seaside city on the Liaodong Peninsula, is the end of the line south from Shenyang.
b22: Hangzhou → Wenzhou · from 1h19 · 163 trains on the day we checked. A coastal line south through Zhejiang to Wenzhou, near the Yandang Mountains.
b23: Qingdao → Yantai · from 1h01 · 38 trains on the day we checked. A ride along the Shandong Peninsula from Qingdao to the seaside city of Yantai.
b24: Journey times and trains per day: Klook search for 27 November 2026. Times change with the day and the train, so check the live schedule when you book.
b26: In second class, seats A and F are by the window (A, B, C on one side, D and F on the other).
b27: Many mountain lines run through long tunnels, so the views come in bursts: keep your camera ready.
b28: Book scenic routes early in spring and autumn, and around Chinese New Year and the October Golden Week.
b29: Some places, like Zhangye and Huangshan, are a bus or taxi ride from the station: plan that leg before you go.
